meta.adoptionDefinition: Mainstream adoption: the year the technology reached widespread, routine use, roughly 10% or more of its potential market or standard practice in its sector.

milestones.title: Nuclear fission to grid power

research.what: Hahn and Strassmann observe fission in Berlin; Meitner and Frisch explain it.

change.what: Calder Hall connects to the UK grid.

milestones.note: War diverted the science into weapons first; civil power came through state programmes.

adoption.what: Nuclear supplies a significant share of electricity in leading economies.

milestones.title: HVDC transmission

research.what: Uno Lamm begins work on high-voltage mercury-arc valves at ASEA.

change.what: Gotland link enters commercial service in Sweden.

milestones.note: A long engineering road from valve research to a dependable link.

milestones.title: Silicon solar cell

research.what: Bell Labs demonstrates the first practical silicon photovoltaic cell.

change.what: Vanguard 1 satellite flies on solar power.

milestones.note: Fast to first use because space could pay any price. Cheap terrestrial solar took another 50 years.

adoption.what: Solar becomes a mainstream source of new power capacity worldwide.

milestones.title: Utility-scale wind

research.what: NASA and the US energy research agency run the MOD-0 turbine programme.

change.what: First commercial wind farm opens in New Hampshire.

milestones.note: Oil shocks gave government research a sharp push into energy.

adoption.what: Wind becomes a mainstream share of new power capacity in Europe and the US.

milestones.title: Lithium-ion battery

research.what: Goodenough’s Oxford group identifies the lithium cobalt oxide cathode.

change.what: Sony launches the first commercial lithium-ion cell.

milestones.note: The same chemistry family later made grid-scale storage viable.

adoption.what: Lithium-ion becomes the standard battery in laptops and mobile phones.

milestones.title: High-temperature superconducting cable

research.what: Bednorz and Müller at IBM Zurich discover high-temperature superconductors.

change.what: A superconducting transmission cable is energised in a US utility grid.

milestones.note: Still niche: cooling, cost and reliability set the pace.

milestones.title: Perovskite solar

research.what: Miyasaka’s group reports perovskite photovoltaic cells.

change.what: First commercial perovskite-on-silicon modules ship.

milestones.note: Durability, not efficiency, set the pace.

milestones.title: Fusion power

research.what: JET, a European publicly funded tokamak at Culham, produces first plasma.

change.what: Not yet landed. UK STEP targets a prototype plant around 2040.

milestones.note: The longest arc in the model and still rising.

milestones.title: Tandem solar at volume

research.what: Perovskite research from 2009, tandem cells from the mid-2010s.

change.what: Perovskite–silicon tandem modules move from niche shipments to volume manufacturing.

milestones.note: Depends on proving 25-year field durability.

basis.label: Industry roadmaps following first commercial shipments (2024)

milestones.title: AI in grid control rooms

research.what: Machine-learning forecasting for wind, solar and demand.

change.what: AI-assisted forecasting and dispatch become routine control room tools, as NESO’s Volta programme (with Alphabet’s Tapestry on the Grand Optimiser) intends.

milestones.note: Assurance, explainability and cyber resilience will set the pace, not model capability.

basis.label: NESO: Volta programme

milestones.title: Household flexibility at scale

research.what: Smart grid and demand response research and trials.

change.what: Batteries, heat pumps and EVs routinely aggregated to support distribution networks.

milestones.note: Turns customers into a network resource; raises new cyber and data questions for DSOs.

milestones.title: Grid-forming inverters as standard

research.what: Academic work on inverters that behave like synchronous machines.

change.what: Grid-forming capability routinely specified on new storage and renewable connections.

milestones.note: Replaces stability services once provided by spinning generators.

milestones.title: Long-duration storage at scale

research.what: Pumped hydro, flow batteries, compressed air and other long-duration technologies proven.

change.what: First GB cap and floor projects (Ofgem Window 1 minded-to decision, June 2026) reach operation.

milestones.note: A case where market design, not research, is the limiting factor.

basis.label: Ofgem: long duration storage Window 1 minded-to decisions

milestones.title: First UK small modular reactors

research.what: SMR competition and regulatory assessment begin.

change.what: Rolls-Royce SMR units at Wylfa well into construction; first power expected mid-2030s.

milestones.note: Lands at the edge of the window. Licensing and supply chain dominate the timeline.

basis.label: Senedd Research: Rolls-Royce SMR at Wylfa

milestones.title: Quantum optimisation pilots

research.what: Academic work on quantum and quantum-inspired grid optimisation.

change.what: Operator pilots for network planning, alongside quantum-inspired classical tools.

milestones.note: Expect quantum-inspired classical methods to deliver value first.

milestones.title: Stored-program computer

research.what: Turing’s paper on computable numbers.

change.what: Ferranti Mark 1 is delivered to the University of Manchester.

milestones.note: Wartime codebreaking compressed the engineering effort.

adoption.what: Computers in widespread use by large businesses and governments.

milestones.title: Transistor

research.what: Bardeen, Brattain and Shockley at Bell Labs.

change.what: Regency TR-1 transistor radio goes on sale.

milestones.note: The classic corporate lab story: basic science and product under one roof.

adoption.what: Transistors replace valves in most new electronics.

milestones.title: Integrated circuit

research.what: Kilby at Texas Instruments, then Noyce at Fairchild.

change.what: First commercial integrated circuits are sold.

milestones.note: Defence and space procurement bought the first chips.

adoption.what: Integrated circuits become standard in computers and electronics.

milestones.title: MOSFET

research.what: Atalla and Kahng demonstrate the MOS transistor at Bell Labs.

change.what: First commercial MOS integrated circuits.

milestones.note: Now the most manufactured device in history.

milestones.title: DRAM

research.what: Dennard invents the one-transistor memory cell at IBM.

change.what: Intel 1103 becomes the first commercial DRAM chip.

milestones.note: Again, a different company reached market first.

milestones.title: Flash memory

research.what: Masuoka presents flash memory at Toshiba.

change.what: First commercial NOR flash chips.

milestones.note: Enabled phones, cameras and solid-state drives.

milestones.title: Giant magnetoresistance

research.what: Fert (Paris-Sud) and Grünberg (Jülich) discover GMR independently.

change.what: IBM ships GMR read heads in hard drives.

milestones.note: A Nobel physics result in every hard drive within a decade.

milestones.title: EUV lithography

research.what: US national laboratories and industry form the EUV LLC research consortium.

change.what: Volume chip production using EUV begins.

milestones.note: Twenty years and enormous capital to make one machine work.

adoption.what: EUV is used for most leading-edge chip production.

milestones.title: GPUs for general computing

research.what: Stanford’s Brook project programs graphics chips for general maths.

change.what: NVIDIA releases CUDA.

milestones.note: The hardware path that later made modern AI possible.

adoption.what: GPUs become standard for scientific and AI computing.

milestones.title: High-NA EUV in volume production

research.what: Development of higher-resolution EUV optics.

change.what: Leading chipmakers use High-NA EUV for volume manufacturing.

milestones.note: Each new tool generation costs more and takes longer.

basis.label: ASML High-NA roadmap

milestones.title: Optical interconnects in AI data centres

research.what: Silicon photonics research.

change.what: Co-packaged optics become common in large AI clusters.

milestones.note: Driven by the power demands of AI, which links back to energy.

milestones.title: Chiplet ecosystems

research.what: Industry work on standard die-to-die interfaces.

change.what: Mix-and-match chiplets from different suppliers in mainstream products.

milestones.note: Shifts hardware supply chain assurance to the package level.

milestones.title: Neuromorphic chips at the edge

research.what: Carver Mead’s neuromorphic engineering at Caltech.

change.what: Brain-inspired, low-power chips in sensors and edge devices.

milestones.note: A 40-year arc that may finally land because of AI energy costs.

milestones.title: High-level programming languages

research.what: Backus proposes FORTRAN at IBM.

change.what: The first FORTRAN compiler ships.

milestones.note: Made programming accessible to scientists and engineers.

milestones.title: Time-sharing

research.what: MIT demonstrates the Compatible Time-Sharing System.

change.what: Commercial time-sharing services launch.

milestones.note: The conceptual ancestor of cloud computing.

milestones.title: Object-oriented programming

research.what: Simula 67 from the Norwegian Computing Center, a public research institute.

change.what: C++ is released commercially.

milestones.note: Ideas can wait years for hardware and markets to catch up.

milestones.title: Unix

research.what: Thompson and Ritchie create Unix at Bell Labs.

change.what: AT&T begins licensing Unix commercially.

milestones.note: Antitrust limits on AT&T shaped how Unix spread.

milestones.title: Relational database

research.what: Codd publishes the relational model at IBM.

change.what: Oracle ships the first commercial SQL database.

milestones.note: A start-up beat the inventing company to market.

adoption.what: Relational databases become the standard for business data.

milestones.title: Graphical interface

research.what: Xerox PARC builds the Alto.

change.what: Xerox Star goes on sale; Apple popularises the idea in 1984.

milestones.note: Invention and commercial success often happen in different companies.

adoption.what: Graphical interfaces become standard on personal computers.

milestones.title: World Wide Web

research.what: Berners-Lee proposes the web at CERN, a publicly funded lab.

change.what: Netscape Navigator is released commercially.

milestones.note: CERN released the technology royalty-free in 1993, which sped everything up.

adoption.what: Most UK and US households use the web.

milestones.title: Open-source operating systems

research.what: Torvalds, a Helsinki student, releases the Linux kernel.

change.what: Commercial Linux distributions are sold with support.

milestones.note: A new model where the research and the product are shared.

adoption.what: Linux runs most of the world’s web servers.

milestones.title: Virtualisation on PCs

research.what: Stanford’s Disco project virtualises commodity hardware.

change.what: VMware, founded by the researchers, ships Workstation.

milestones.note: The foundation of cloud computing.

milestones.title: Large-scale data processing

research.what: Google publishes MapReduce.

change.what: Managed big-data services offered by cloud providers.

milestones.note: Open-source reimplementation moved it out of Google.

milestones.title: AI writes most new code

research.what: Code-generating language models.

change.what: In many organisations most new code is drafted by AI and reviewed by people.

milestones.note: Software assurance and supply chain security must adapt.

milestones.title: Agent interoperability standards

research.what: Protocols for connecting AI agents to tools and data.

change.what: Common standards let agents work across vendors’ systems.

milestones.note: Identity and authorisation for agents become critical controls.

milestones.title: Memory-safe languages by default

research.what: Rust and similar languages emerge from industry research.

change.what: New critical systems code is written in memory-safe languages by default.

milestones.note: Backed by government security agency guidance.

milestones.title: AI-assisted formal verification

research.what: Machine learning applied to mathematical proof of program correctness.

change.what: Routine proofs of correctness for critical components.

milestones.note: Could change how safety-critical software is assured.

milestones.title: Expert systems

research.what: DENDRAL at Stanford encodes expert chemistry knowledge.

change.what: XCON goes into operational use at Digital Equipment Corporation.

milestones.note: Early AI that worked, then hit the limits of hand-written rules.

milestones.title: Statistical speech recognition

research.what: IBM’s statistical approach to speech recognition.

change.what: Continuous-speech dictation software goes on sale.

milestones.note: Computing power, not ideas, was the bottleneck.

milestones.title: Neural networks in products

research.what: Rumelhart, Hinton and Williams popularise backpropagation.

change.what: Neural networks read handwritten cheques in commercial banking systems.

milestones.note: Worked in a niche, then went quiet for 15 years.

milestones.title: Deep learning for images

research.what: AlexNet from the University of Toronto wins ImageNet.

change.what: Deep-learning photo search appears in Google’s products.

milestones.note: Google acquired the team, a pattern that became common.

adoption.what: Deep learning becomes standard in image recognition products.

milestones.title: Transformer models

research.what: Google researchers publish the transformer architecture.

change.what: Transformer models enter Google Search ranking.

milestones.note: From here on, research and product cycles in AI largely merge.

adoption.what: Transformer models power everyday products used by hundreds of millions of people.

milestones.title: Learning from human feedback

research.what: Researchers show models can learn from human preference ratings.

change.what: ChatGPT launches.

milestones.note: The method that made language models usable by the public.

adoption.what: Used to train most widely deployed AI assistants.

milestones.title: Diffusion image generation

research.what: Berkeley researchers publish denoising diffusion models.

change.what: Public text-to-image services launch.

milestones.note: Two years from paper to mass use.

milestones.title: Reasoning models

research.what: Chain-of-thought research shows step-by-step reasoning gains.

change.what: Commercial reasoning models are released.

milestones.note: Months, not years, between paper and product.

milestones.title: Agentic AI in everyday work

research.what: Tool-using and planning language model research.

change.what: AI agents routinely complete multi-step tasks inside enterprise systems.

milestones.note: Governance, identity and access control become the bottleneck.

milestones.title: On-device AI as default

research.what: Efficient neural networks and neural processing units.

change.what: Capable AI runs locally on most new phones and laptops.

milestones.note: Shifts some risk from the cloud to the endpoint.

milestones.title: EU high-risk AI rules apply

research.what: European Commission proposes the AI Act.

change.what: High-risk obligations for stand-alone systems apply from 2 December 2027, after the 2026 Digital Omnibus delay.

milestones.note: Change also means regulation: here the gap is set by law-making, not research.

basis.label: EU AI Act Digital Omnibus: postponed high-risk deadlines

milestones.title: AI as a scientific collaborator

research.what: AI systems that generate and test scientific hypotheses.

change.what: AI-originated results are routine in peer-reviewed science.

milestones.note: Could compress research gaps in every other lane.

milestones.title: Atomic clock

research.what: Rabi proposes atomic-beam clocks at Columbia; NPL builds a caesium clock in 1955.

change.what: The first commercial caesium clock goes on sale.

milestones.note: First-generation quantum technology now underpins GPS and the grid’s timing.

adoption.what: Atomic time defines the SI second and underpins national time services.

milestones.title: Laser

research.what: Schawlow and Townes publish the laser principle (Bell Labs, Columbia).

change.what: Commercial lasers go on sale.

milestones.note: Called a solution looking for a problem; now everywhere.

adoption.what: Lasers appear in everyday products such as barcode scanners and CD players.

milestones.title: Quantum key distribution

research.what: Bennett (IBM) and Brassard (Montréal) publish BB84.

change.what: First commercial QKD systems go on sale.

milestones.note: Real but niche; national security agencies favour post-quantum cryptography.

milestones.title: Quantum annealing

research.what: MIT researchers propose adiabatic quantum computing.

change.what: D-Wave sells its first quantum annealer.

milestones.note: Commercial before it was clearly useful.

milestones.title: Quantum computing access

research.what: NEC demonstrates a superconducting qubit.

change.what: IBM opens cloud access to a small quantum processor.

milestones.note: A product for learning and research, not yet for advantage.

milestones.title: Quantum gravimeter

research.what: Stanford demonstrates atom interferometry.

change.what: Commercial atom-interferometer gravimeters go on sale.

milestones.note: Quantum sensing is arriving before quantum computing.

milestones.title: Cryptographically relevant quantum computer

research.what: Shor, at Bell Labs, shows quantum computers could break public-key cryptography.

change.what: Not yet landed. Timelines are uncertain and widely debated.

milestones.note: Uncertainty about when is exactly why migration has to start now.

milestones.title: Verified quantum advantage

research.what: Superconducting and other qubit platforms since the late 1990s.

change.what: Independently verified advantage on scientific problems; IBM expects first examples in 2026.

milestones.note: Expect claims and counter-claims as classical methods improve too.

basis.label: IBM quantum roadmap (advantage by end of 2026)

milestones.title: Fault-tolerant quantum computer

research.what: Error-correction research since the 1990s.

change.what: IBM targets Starling, with 200 logical qubits, for 2029.

milestones.note: A vendor roadmap. Previous roadmaps have slipped.

basis.label: IBM quantum roadmap (Starling, 2029 target)

milestones.title: Quantum navigation in service

research.what: Atom interferometry and cold-atom sensing.

change.what: Quantum navigation trialled operationally as a backup when satellite navigation is jammed or spoofed.

milestones.note: A UK national quantum mission; relevant to timing-dependent infrastructure.

basis.label: UK National Quantum Strategy missions

milestones.title: Machine codebreaking

research.what: Turing and Welchman design the Bombe at Bletchley Park.

change.what: First Bombe goes into operational use.

milestones.note: Wartime urgency: research to operations in months.

milestones.title: Public-key cryptography (secret)

research.what: Ellis and Cocks at GCHQ invent non-secret encryption.

change.what: GCHQ publicly discloses the work.

milestones.note: Classified research can be decades ahead of the market and never reach it.

milestones.title: Public-key cryptography (open)

research.what: Diffie and Hellman at Stanford; RSA at MIT a year later.

change.what: RSA Data Security ships its first commercial products.

milestones.note: Became the foundation of e-commerce and online banking.

adoption.what: Public-key encryption secures most web commerce.

milestones.title: Antivirus

research.what: Cohen’s research defines the computer virus.

change.what: First commercial antivirus products launch.

milestones.note: The threat arrived quickly, so the market did too.

milestones.title: Intrusion detection

research.what: Denning’s intrusion detection model at SRI, publicly funded.

change.what: Commercial network intrusion detection products reach the market.

milestones.note: Government-funded research seeded much of today’s security monitoring.

milestones.title: Firewall

research.what: Packet-filtering research at Digital Equipment Corporation.

change.what: DEC delivers the first commercial firewall, later sold as DEC SEAL, on 13 June 1991.

milestones.note: Internet growth turned research into a product line within three years.

provenance.qaNote: All cited links are broken; downgraded until a new source is found.

adoption.what: Firewalls become standard for business networks.

milestones.title: Industrial control system security

research.what: Aurora test at Idaho National Laboratory shows a cyber attack can destroy a generator.

change.what: Dedicated OT network monitoring products appear.

milestones.note: Stuxnet in 2010 turned a lab demonstration into a market.

adoption.what: Security monitoring becomes common practice in critical infrastructure networks.

milestones.title: Homomorphic encryption

research.what: Gentry’s first fully homomorphic scheme, Stanford.

change.what: Production-grade libraries released for commercial use.

milestones.note: Still slow, but useful for privacy-preserving analytics.

milestones.title: Zero trust

research.what: Forrester defines the zero trust model; Google begins BeyondCorp.

change.what: Commercial zero trust access services launch.

milestones.note: Now embedded in government guidance worldwide.

milestones.title: Post-quantum cryptography

research.what: NIST opens its post-quantum standardisation process.

change.what: FIPS 203–205 published; hybrid post-quantum key exchange on by default in major browsers.

milestones.note: Standards and early deployment arrived together.

adoption.what: Hybrid post-quantum key exchange protects a large share of web traffic.

milestones.title: AI vulnerability discovery

research.what: DARPA Cyber Grand Challenge pits autonomous systems against each other.

change.what: AI systems find real vulnerabilities in widely used software; AIxCC tools released.

milestones.note: Helps defenders and attackers alike.

milestones.title: Post-quantum migration of priority systems

research.what: Post-quantum standardisation from 2016.

change.what: NCSC guidance sets 2031 for completing migration of the highest-priority systems.

milestones.note: Owners of long-lived operational technology need to plan now.

basis.label: NCSC: Timelines for migration to post-quantum cryptography (2031 milestone)

milestones.title: AI agents in security operations

research.what: Language models applied to alert triage and investigation.

change.what: Most first-line alert triage is handled by AI agents under human oversight.

milestones.note: Analyst skills shift toward supervision and threat hunting.

milestones.title: Exploit windows collapse

research.what: AI-assisted code analysis and exploit research.

change.what: Time from disclosure to exploitation falls to days or hours for many flaws.

milestones.note: Patching and compensating controls for operational technology need rethinking.

milestones.title: Automated vulnerability repair

research.what: DARPA challenges on autonomous find-and-fix.

change.what: AI-generated patches become standard in mainstream software maintenance.

milestones.note: Assurance of AI-written fixes becomes a new discipline.

milestones.title: AI anomaly detection in OT networks

research.what: OT monitoring and machine learning anomaly detection.

change.what: AI-assisted detection is standard across energy network control systems.

milestones.note: False positives in safety-critical settings are the hard problem.

milestones.title: Television

research.what: Baird demonstrates television in London.

change.what: The BBC starts a regular high-definition television service.

milestones.note: A public broadcaster turned an inventor’s demo into a service.

adoption.what: Most UK households have a television.

milestones.title: Radar

research.what: Watson-Watt’s Daventry experiment for the Air Ministry.

change.what: Chain Home radar stations become operational.

milestones.note: Threat of war produced one of the fastest arcs of the century.

adoption.what: Radar becomes standard in military and civil aviation.

milestones.title: Cellular networks

research.what: Bell Labs engineers set out the cellular concept.

change.what: The first commercial cellular network opens in Tokyo.

milestones.note: Thirty years, largely waiting for spectrum allocation and electronics. Regulators can set the clock.

adoption.what: Mobile phones are widely owned in leading economies.

milestones.title: Communications satellites

research.what: Pierce at Bell Labs proposes orbital radio relays.

change.what: Intelsat I begins commercial service.

milestones.note: The space race supplied the launchers.

milestones.title: LDPC error-correcting codes

research.what: Gallager invents LDPC codes at MIT.

change.what: LDPC codes adopted in satellite TV standards, then Wi-Fi and 5G.

milestones.note: Forgotten for 30 years until rediscovered at Cambridge in the 1990s.

milestones.title: Optical fibre

research.what: Kao and Hockham at STL, Harlow, show low-loss glass fibre is possible.

change.what: First commercial fibre links carry live traffic.

milestones.note: British research, Nobel prize, global backbone.

adoption.what: Fibre carries most long-distance telecoms traffic.

milestones.title: Wi-Fi technology

research.what: CSIRO, Australia’s public research agency, patents its wireless LAN technique.

change.what: High-speed Wi-Fi products using the technique go on sale.

milestones.note: Radio astronomy research ended up in billions of devices.

adoption.what: Wi-Fi becomes standard in homes and laptops.

milestones.title: MIMO wireless

research.what: Paulraj and Kailath at Stanford patent spatial multiplexing.

change.what: First MIMO Wi-Fi chipsets ship.

milestones.note: Behind every modern Wi-Fi and mobile network.

milestones.title: Massive MIMO

research.what: Marzetta at Bell Labs proposes very large antenna arrays.

change.what: SoftBank in Japan launches the first commercial Massive MIMO service on its 4G/pre-5G network; it later becomes standard in 5G.

milestones.note: Standards cycles set the pace for telecoms.

milestones.title: Satellite direct to phones

research.what: Research on satellites talking to ordinary handsets.

change.what: Messaging and basic data from satellites to standard phones become mainstream.

milestones.note: A new layer of resilience for remote network assets.

milestones.title: First 6G networks

research.what: 6G research programmes in academia and industry.

change.what: First commercial 6G services launch.

milestones.note: Expect sensing, AI-native operation and security by design to feature.

basis.label: 3GPP 6G timeline: first specifications around 2028–29

milestones.title: Polyethylene

research.what: Fawcett and Gibson at ICI discover polyethylene.

change.what: Commercial production begins; vital for radar cable insulation.

milestones.note: A lab accident that became the world’s most common plastic.

milestones.title: Nylon

research.what: Carothers’ team at DuPont makes nylon.

change.what: First nylon products go on sale; stockings follow in 1940.

milestones.note: Corporate labs at their fastest.

adoption.what: Nylon is widely used in clothing and consumer goods.

milestones.title: PTFE (Teflon)

research.what: Plunkett discovers PTFE at DuPont.

change.what: PTFE products are sold commercially.

milestones.note: War production came before consumer use.

milestones.title: Carbon fibre

research.what: Watt, Johnson and Phillips at RAE Farnborough.

change.what: British firms begin commercial production.

milestones.note: UK government research created a global industry.

adoption.what: Carbon fibre enters mainstream airliner structures.

milestones.title: Kevlar

research.what: Kwolek discovers aramid fibre at DuPont.

change.what: Kevlar is commercialised.

milestones.note: Now in body armour and high-voltage cable reinforcement.

milestones.title: Stable liquid crystals

research.what: Gray’s team at the University of Hull, funded by the UK defence ministry.

change.what: Liquid crystal displays in watches and calculators.

milestones.note: Fast because a clear customer need was defined up front.

milestones.title: Blue LED

research.what: Akasaki and Amano make p-type gallium nitride in Nagoya.

change.what: Nichia launches the bright blue LED.

milestones.note: Enabled white LED lighting, a large global energy saving.

adoption.what: LED lighting becomes mainstream in homes and streets.

milestones.title: Metal-organic frameworks

research.what: Yaghi’s group reports the MOF-5 framework.

change.what: First commercial MOF product used in fruit storage.

milestones.note: Honoured with the 2025 Nobel Prize in Chemistry; carbon capture is the next test.

milestones.title: Metamaterials

research.what: Pendry at Imperial College describes the perfect lens.

change.what: Metamaterial satellite antennas reach the market.

milestones.note: Theory first, engineering second.

milestones.title: Graphene

research.what: Geim and Novoselov isolate graphene at Manchester.

change.what: First consumer products with graphene additives.

milestones.note: Big promise, slower industrial impact than expected.

milestones.title: Sodium-ion batteries

research.what: Renewed academic research on sodium-ion electrodes.

change.what: First production cars with sodium-ion batteries.

milestones.note: Cheaper, abundant materials, less exposed to lithium supply.

milestones.title: Solid-state batteries in production cars

research.what: Tokyo Tech reports a fast lithium-ion solid conductor.

change.what: Small-volume production in premium electric vehicles; makers target 2027–28.

milestones.note: Volume and cost, not chemistry, are now the limits.

basis.label: Manufacturer targets (Toyota, Samsung SDI): 2027–28

milestones.title: Sodium-ion grid storage at scale

research.what: Sodium-ion electrode research and first products.

change.what: Large sodium-ion installations on electricity networks.

milestones.note: Diversifies storage supply chains.

milestones.title: MOFs for carbon capture

research.what: Metal-organic framework research.

change.what: Commercial-scale carbon capture using MOF sorbents.

milestones.note: Cost and durability at industrial scale still to be shown.

milestones.title: AI-discovered materials in products

research.what: AI models predict hundreds of thousands of new stable crystals.

change.what: A commercial product built on an AI-discovered material.

milestones.note: Synthesis and testing remain slow, physical steps.

milestones.title: Liquid-fuelled rocket to orbit

research.what: Goddard launches the first liquid-fuelled rocket in Massachusetts.

change.what: Sputnik becomes the first artificial satellite.

milestones.note: Government programmes did the scaling.

adoption.what: Routine satellite launches for communications and weather.

milestones.title: Commercial Earth observation

research.what: NASA launches Landsat 1.

change.what: SPOT 1 begins selling satellite imagery commercially.

milestones.note: Now central to network monitoring, vegetation management and climate data.

adoption.what: Satellite imagery enters everyday use through online maps.

milestones.title: Satellite navigation

research.what: US Department of Defense approves the GPS programme.

change.what: First handheld commercial GPS receiver.

milestones.note: Full civilian accuracy only arrived in 2000. Grid timing now depends on it.

adoption.what: Satellite navigation becomes standard in cars and smartphones.

milestones.title: Reusable rockets

research.what: DC-X vertical-landing demonstrator, US defence funded.

change.what: A Falcon 9 booster is reflown commercially.

milestones.note: Government proved the idea; a company proved the economics.

adoption.what: Most launches to orbit use reusable boosters.

milestones.title: CubeSats

research.what: Stanford and Cal Poly define the CubeSat standard.

change.what: Commercial imaging constellations of small satellites deploy.

milestones.note: Standardisation cut the cost of reaching orbit.

milestones.title: Low-orbit satellite broadband

research.what: Teledesic proposes a broadband constellation.

change.what: Starlink opens public service.

milestones.note: The first attempt failed; cheap launch made the second work.

milestones.title: In-orbit satellite servicing

research.what: DARPA’s Orbital Express demonstrates robotic servicing.

change.what: A commercial servicing vehicle docks to extend a satellite’s life.

milestones.note: Space is becoming maintainable infrastructure.

milestones.title: Fully reusable heavy launch

research.what: Development of fully reusable launch systems.

change.what: Routine operational flights with both stages recovered.

milestones.note: Would cut launch costs again, by a large factor.

milestones.title: In-orbit refuelling

research.what: Robotic servicing research.

change.what: Commercial refuelling of satellites in orbit.

milestones.note: Extends asset lives, raises new security questions.

milestones.title: Space-based solar power demonstration

research.what: Glaser proposes space-based solar power.

change.what: Power beamed from orbit to the ground in a meaningful demonstration.

milestones.note: A 60-year arc. Still a demonstration, not a power source.

milestones.title: Industrial robot

research.what: Devol files his patent for a programmable manipulator.

change.what: Unimate starts work on a General Motors line.

milestones.note: Automation entered factories within a decade.

adoption.what: Robots become standard on car production lines.

milestones.title: Home robots

research.what: Brooks’ behaviour-based robotics at MIT.

change.what: The Roomba vacuum cleaner goes on sale.

milestones.note: The first mass-market robot was deliberately simple.

milestones.title: Surgical robots

research.what: SRI telepresence surgery research, defence funded.

change.what: A robotic surgical system is cleared for use in the US.

milestones.note: Medical regulation lengthened the arc.

milestones.title: Driverless cars

research.what: DARPA Grand Challenge for autonomous vehicles.

change.what: Fully driverless robotaxi rides open to the public in Arizona.

milestones.note: Government prize money created an industry.

milestones.title: Consumer drones

research.what: University research on stable autonomous quadrotor control.

change.what: Ready-to-fly camera drones go on sale.

milestones.note: Dates approximate. Cheap phone sensors did the rest.

refs.label: DJI press release: Phantom launch (7 Jan 2013)

milestones.title: UK robotaxis

research.what: Wayve spins out of Cambridge with end-to-end driving AI.

change.what: Supervised autonomous Uber rides launch across London in September 2026.

milestones.note: UK legislation, the Automated Vehicles Act 2024, set the route to market.

refs.label: Wayve and Uber London service announcements (2026)

milestones.title: Fully driverless rides in London

research.what: Autonomous driving research and supervised service.

change.what: Paid rides with no safety driver on board.

milestones.note: Depends on full deployment rules under the Automated Vehicles Act.

basis.label: Wayve and Uber London supervised service (2026) and Automated Vehicles Act

milestones.title: Humanoid robots at work

research.what: Humanoid research from the early 2000s.

change.what: Paid humanoid deployments in warehouses and factories, in small numbers.

milestones.note: Expect pilots to outnumber real deployments for some time.

milestones.title: Routine beyond-sight drone inspection

research.what: Autonomous inspection drone research and trials.

change.what: Drones routinely inspect power lines beyond the pilot’s line of sight.

milestones.note: Directly relevant to network operators; airspace rules set the pace.

milestones.title: Penicillin

research.what: Fleming observes penicillin at St Mary’s Hospital, London.

change.what: Mass production for Allied forces.

milestones.note: Fifteen years, and a war, to get from discovery to scale.

adoption.what: Penicillin becomes widely available for civilian use.

refs.label: CDC Emerging Infectious Diseases: The Discovery of Penicillin (2017)

milestones.title: Recombinant DNA

research.what: Cohen and Boyer, Stanford and UCSF.

change.what: Recombinant human insulin is approved.

milestones.note: Launched the biotech industry.

adoption.what: Recombinant medicines such as insulin become standard treatments.

refs.label: Science History Institute: Herbert W. Boyer and Stanley N. Cohen

milestones.title: MRI scanning

research.what: Lauterbur publishes magnetic resonance imaging; Mansfield develops it at Nottingham.

change.what: The first commercial MRI scanner.

milestones.note: Quantum physics in every hospital.

adoption.what: MRI becomes standard in hospitals.

milestones.title: Monoclonal antibodies

research.what: Köhler and Milstein at the MRC Laboratory of Molecular Biology, Cambridge.

change.what: First monoclonal antibody therapy is approved.

milestones.note: Not patented, which some still debate.

refs.label: An (2017), Protein & Cell: 'Magic Bullets' special issue on therapeutic antibodies

milestones.title: PCR

research.what: Mullis at Cetus Corporation.

change.what: Commercial PCR instruments and kits are sold.

milestones.note: Lab tools move faster than medicines.

refs.label: Thermo Fisher: PCR thermal cycler history

milestones.title: Genome sequencing to consumers

research.what: Human Genome Project begins.

change.what: Direct-to-consumer genetic testing launches.

milestones.note: Sequencing costs fell faster than Moore’s law.

milestones.title: mRNA vaccines

research.what: Karikó and Weissman’s modified nucleoside work, University of Pennsylvania.

change.what: First mRNA vaccine is authorised.

milestones.note: Fifteen years of slow research, then less than a year to authorisation.

adoption.what: Billions of doses are given worldwide.

milestones.title: CRISPR gene editing

research.what: Doudna and Charpentier publish programmable CRISPR-Cas9.

change.what: First CRISPR therapy approved, by the UK regulator first.

milestones.note: Fast for a medicine; regulation still sets the floor.

refs.label: HLK: Casgevy world's first CRISPR approval

milestones.title: Protein structure prediction

research.what: AlphaFold 2 from DeepMind wins CASP14.

change.what: Open AlphaFold database of predicted structures released.

milestones.note: Software-speed delivery in a physical science.

adoption.what: Predicted structures are used routinely by most biology labs.

refs.label: EMBL: AlphaFold Nobel and database history

milestones.title: AI-discovered medicines

research.what: AI-designed drug candidates enter clinical trials.

change.what: First approval of a medicine where AI designed the molecule.

milestones.note: AI shortens discovery, not clinical trials.

milestones.title: In-body gene editing

research.what: Delivery of editing tools directly into the body.

change.what: First approval of an in vivo gene-editing therapy.

milestones.note: Safety findings could move this either way.

milestones.title: Computer weather forecasting

research.what: First computer weather forecast on ENIAC by Charney and von Neumann’s publicly funded team.

change.what: Operational numerical weather prediction begins.

milestones.note: Sweden (Rossby's group at SMHI) produced an operational numerical forecast in 1954; US operational NWP began in 1955 under the JNWPU.

milestones.title: Power system state estimation

research.what: Schweppe at MIT publishes state estimation for power networks.

change.what: Energy management systems with state estimation enter control rooms.

milestones.note: The first time software, not just operators, built a live picture of the grid.

milestones.title: Synchrophasor measurement

research.what: Phadke and Thorp build the phasor measurement unit at Virginia Tech.

change.what: First commercial phasor measurement units.

milestones.note: High-speed grid data: one of the foundations the vision says AI depends on.

milestones.title: Wind power forecasting

research.what: Risø, the Danish national laboratory, develops statistical wind power prediction.

change.what: DTU's Wind Power Prediction Tool (WPPT) enters operational use in Elsam/Eltra control rooms in western Denmark.

milestones.note: Forecasting was the first job machine learning did for renewables.

milestones.title: Wind turbine predictive maintenance

research.what: Academic work on machine learning from turbine SCADA and vibration data.

change.what: Commercial predictive maintenance services for wind fleets. Dates approximate.

milestones.note: One of the vision’s near-term areas, already common in generation.

refs.label: CORDIS: Providing Predictive Maintenance for Wind Turbines Over Cloud (2015)

milestones.title: AI data centre cooling

research.what: Google researchers model data centre efficiency with neural networks.

change.what: DeepMind control cuts Google data centre cooling energy.

milestones.note: An early proof that AI can cut end-use energy at scale.

milestones.title: Smart EV charging

research.what: Academic research on optimised and price-responsive EV charging.

change.what: Supplier-managed smart EV charging tariffs reach GB households at scale.

milestones.note: The vision names EV charging as an area where AI is already used.

milestones.title: Machine learning solar nowcasting

research.what: Open Climate Fix, a UK non-profit, develops machine learning solar forecasts.

change.what: Its forecasts are used by the GB system operator’s control room.

milestones.note: A UK example of research reaching the control room in about four years.

milestones.title: A largely self-running energy system

research.what: Agentic AI research; the DESNZ vision’s stretching scenario of AI agents coordinating every asset.

change.what: Not landed. DESNZ treats it as one plausible future, not a prediction.

milestones.note: Raises the vision’s hardest questions: oversight, accountability, concentration and skills.

milestones.title: AI predictive maintenance across networks

research.what: Condition monitoring and machine learning on network asset data.

change.what: AI-driven maintenance routine for transformers, cables and overhead lines.

milestones.note: Fewer faults and less premature replacement, two of the vision’s goals.

milestones.title: Self-updating network digital twins

research.what: Digital twin and network modelling research.

change.what: Live digital twins continuously reassess where reinforcement is needed.

milestones.note: The vision flags tension with planning and consenting built around fixed decision points.

milestones.title: AI assurance for energy

research.what: Ofgem’s ethical AI guidance, AI Regulatory Laboratory and technical sandbox.

change.what: Sector-specific, system-level assurance for AI in operational decisions.

milestones.note: The vision names regulatory clarity and assurance as key barriers to adoption.

basis.label: DESNZ: Vision for an AI-enabled clean energy system

milestones.title: AI for Clean Energy Strategy

research.what: Lucy Yu’s review of AI in electricity networks and the DESNZ vision call for evidence (closes 6 November 2026).

change.what: The UK’s first AI for Clean Energy Strategy, designed to be updated iteratively.

milestones.note: Policy itself is being designed to keep pace with fast change.

basis.label: DESNZ: Vision for an AI-enabled clean energy system

milestones.title: Machine-speed flexibility markets

research.what: Research on automated, local flexibility trading.

change.what: Automated agents trade household and business flexibility in granular local markets.

milestones.note: The vision asks whether current market design can support coordination at machine speed.

milestones.title: AI plasma control for fusion

research.what: DeepMind and EPFL control a tokamak plasma with reinforcement learning.

change.what: AI control routinely used on fusion experiments.

milestones.note: The vision cites AI for Science support for fusion, including at Culham.

milestones.title: Combined-cycle gas turbine

research.what: Brown Boveri builds the first utility gas turbine.

change.what: Combined-cycle plants enter commercial service. Dates approximate.

milestones.note: The technology behind the 1990s dash for gas.

milestones.title: Grid-scale lithium-ion storage

research.what: Commercial lithium-ion cells from 1991.

change.what: Large grid batteries provide fast frequency response at scale.

milestones.note: Cost decline, not invention, closed this gap.

adoption.what: Batteries become a mainstream part of new grid capacity in GB, the US and Australia.

milestones.title: Magnetic core memory

research.what: Forrester’s team at MIT, defence funded.

change.what: Core memory in commercial computers.

milestones.note: Dominated computer memory for 20 years.

milestones.title: Hard disk drive

research.what: IBM San Jose begins disk storage research.

change.what: IBM RAMAC ships with the first hard disk.

milestones.note: Five megabytes, the size of two fridges.

milestones.title: CMOS logic

research.what: Wanlass at Fairchild invents CMOS.

change.what: First commercial CMOS integrated circuits.

milestones.note: Low-power logic that every modern chip uses.

milestones.title: Microprocessor

research.what: Hoff, Faggin and Mazor design a CPU on one chip at Intel.

change.what: Intel 4004 goes on sale.

milestones.note: Built for a calculator maker.

adoption.what: Microprocessors are in most new electronics and computers.

milestones.title: RISC processors

research.what: Berkeley RISC and Stanford MIPS projects.

change.what: Acorn Archimedes ships with the ARM processor.

milestones.note: ARM, born in Cambridge, now powers almost every phone.

milestones.title: FinFET transistors

research.what: Hu and colleagues at Berkeley, DARPA funded.

change.what: Intel ships 22 nm 3D transistors.

milestones.note: Kept Moore’s law going for another decade.

milestones.title: Utility and cloud computing

research.what: McCarthy at MIT proposes computing sold like a utility.

change.what: Amazon Web Services launches on-demand cloud services.

milestones.note: A 45-year arc waiting for networks and economics.

adoption.what: Most businesses use cloud services.

milestones.title: Blockchain

research.what: Haber and Stornetta at Bellcore publish tamper-evident time-stamping.

change.what: Bitcoin launches.

milestones.note: Cited in the original Bitcoin paper.

milestones.title: Web search ranking

research.what: Page and Brin develop PageRank at Stanford.

change.what: Google launches as a company.

milestones.note: Two years from PhD project to product.

milestones.title: Statistical machine translation

research.what: IBM’s Candide project models translation statistically.

change.what: Google Translate launches.

milestones.note: Data, not linguistics, won.

milestones.title: Recommender systems

research.what: GroupLens collaborative filtering at the University of Minnesota.

change.what: Amazon deploys item-to-item recommendations.

milestones.note: Quietly one of the most profitable AI applications.

milestones.title: LSTM networks

research.what: Hochreiter and Schmidhuber publish LSTM in Munich.

change.what: LSTM speech recognition deployed in Google’s products.

milestones.note: Eighteen years waiting for data and GPUs.

milestones.title: Voice assistants

research.what: DARPA’s CALO personal assistant programme at SRI.

change.what: Siri, an SRI spin-out, ships on the iPhone.

milestones.note: Defence research reaches every pocket in eight years.

milestones.title: SQUID magnetometers

research.what: Ford Research Laboratory demonstrates the superconducting quantum interference device.

change.what: Commercial SQUID magnetometers. Dates approximate.

milestones.note: Quantum sensing has a 60-year commercial history.

milestones.title: Trapped-ion quantum computing

research.what: Cirac and Zoller propose trapped-ion quantum logic.

change.what: Trapped-ion quantum computers available through public clouds.

milestones.note: Spun out of university and national laboratory research.

milestones.title: Data Encryption Standard

research.what: IBM’s Lucifer cipher (Feistel).

change.what: DES becomes a US federal standard.

milestones.note: The first public, standardised commercial cipher.

milestones.title: AES encryption

research.what: Daemen and Rijmen at KU Leuven submit Rijndael.

change.what: Published as the AES standard.

milestones.note: Open competition delivered a trusted standard in three years.

milestones.title: Passkeys

research.what: The FIDO Alliance forms to replace passwords with public-key credentials.

change.what: Passkeys launch across major platforms.

milestones.note: Standards and ecosystem alignment set this pace.

milestones.title: Packet switching

research.what: Davies at the National Physical Laboratory, alongside Baran at RAND.

change.what: First commercial packet-switched networks open.

milestones.note: A British government laboratory helped invent how the internet moves data.

milestones.title: TCP/IP

research.what: Cerf and Kahn publish the internet protocol design, DARPA funded.

change.what: First commercial internet service providers.

milestones.note: Fifteen years inside publicly funded networks.

adoption.what: Internet protocols carry most data traffic.

milestones.title: GSM mobile

research.what: European telecoms administrations form the GSM group.

change.what: First GSM call on a commercial network.

milestones.note: A common standard made Europe a mobile leader.

adoption.what: GSM becomes the world’s dominant mobile standard.

milestones.title: Bluetooth

research.what: Ericsson begins short-range radio research.

change.what: First Bluetooth products ship.

milestones.note: Industry consortia can move fast.

milestones.title: Shape-memory alloy

research.what: US Naval Ordnance Laboratory discovers nitinol.

change.what: First commercial medical uses. Dates approximate.

milestones.note: Now in stents, actuators and couplings.

milestones.title: Strengthened glass

research.what: Corning’s Project Muscle creates chemically strengthened glass.

change.what: Used as the cover glass of the first iPhone.

milestones.note: A 45-year arc: the material waited for its product.

milestones.title: Neodymium magnets

research.what: General Motors and Sumitomo independently develop NdFeB magnets.

change.what: Commercial production begins.

milestones.note: Essential to wind turbines and electric vehicles today.

adoption.what: Standard magnets in hard drives, motors and later wind turbines.

milestones.title: Electric propulsion

research.what: Kaufman at NASA builds the gridded ion thruster.

change.what: Ion thrusters used on commercial communications satellites.

milestones.note: Nearly 40 years, then standard.

milestones.title: Satellite television

research.what: Telstar relays the first transatlantic television.

change.what: Commercial satellite distribution of cable TV channels begins.

milestones.note: Turned broadcasting into a global industry.

milestones.title: Robot mapping (SLAM)

change.what: Visual SLAM ships in consumer home robots.

milestones.title: Warehouse robots

change.what: First commercial warehouse deployments.

milestones.title: Spinning lidar

milestones.note: A government prize created a sensor industry.

milestones.title: DNA sequencing

research.what: Sanger publishes chain-termination sequencing at the MRC LMB, Cambridge.

milestones.note: Two Nobel prizes for Sanger.

milestones.title: Statins

research.what: Endo at Sankyo discovers the first statin.

change.what: Lovastatin is approved.

milestones.note: Typical of medicines: about 14 years.

refs.label: Lasker Foundation: Getting to the Heart of Cardiovascular Disease

milestones.title: Next-generation sequencing

research.what: Balasubramanian and Klenerman at Cambridge invent Solexa sequencing.

change.what: First commercial Solexa sequencer.

milestones.note: A UK invention that cut genome costs a million-fold.

milestones.note: The first “killer app” that sold personal computers.

milestones.title: PostScript and desktop publishing

research.what: Warnock and Geschke work on page description languages at Xerox PARC.

change.what: PostScript ships in the Apple LaserWriter.

refs.label: Computer History Museum: Charles M. Geschke

milestones.title: Microsoft Windows

research.what: Microsoft starts its Interface Manager project.

change.what: Windows 1.0 is released.

milestones.note: Popularised graphical computing on IBM-compatible PCs.

milestones.title: Software as a service

change.what: Its subscription CRM service launches.

milestones.note: Turned software from a licence into a subscription.

refs.label: Reference for Business: History of salesforce.com

milestones.title: Social networking

research.what: Zuckerberg’s Facemash project at Harvard.

change.what: TheFacebook launches to Harvard students, then the world.

milestones.note: A student project to a global platform in a few years.

change.what: YouTube opens to the public.

milestones.title: Microblogging

research.what: Dorsey proposes a status-sharing service inside podcast company Odeo.

change.what: Twitter launches publicly.

milestones.note: From internal hack to public product in months.

milestones.title: Music streaming

research.what: Spotify is founded in Stockholm.

change.what: The streaming service launches in Europe.

milestones.note: Licensing, not technology, set the pace.

milestones.title: Mobile photo sharing

research.what: Systrom and Krieger pivot their app Burbn to photos.

change.what: Instagram launches on the iPhone.

milestones.note: Sold to Facebook for $1bn 18 months later.

milestones.title: Workplace messaging

research.what: Tiny Speck builds an internal chat tool while making a game.

change.what: Slack launches publicly.

milestones.note: A side project that outgrew the main product.

milestones.title: IBM System/360

research.what: IBM’s SPREAD committee defines a compatible family of computers.

change.what: First System/360 machines are delivered.

milestones.note: Created the idea of a compatible computer architecture.

milestones.title: Cray-1 supercomputer

research.what: Seymour Cray founds Cray Research.

change.what: Cray-1 is delivered to Los Alamos.

milestones.note: Supercomputers later became essential to weather and grid modelling.

milestones.title: Apple II personal computer

research.what: Wozniak designs the Apple I.

change.what: The Apple II goes on sale.

milestones.note: Personal computing becomes a consumer product.

milestones.title: IBM PC

research.what: IBM’s Project Chess team in Boca Raton.

change.what: The IBM PC launches.

milestones.note: Open architecture created the PC industry.

milestones.title: Pure-play chip foundry

change.what: TSMC begins manufacturing chips for other companies.

milestones.note: Government research created the company most chips now depend on.

milestones.title: iPhone

research.what: Apple’s Project Purple begins.

change.what: The iPhone launches.

milestones.note: Combined decades of research into one product.

milestones.title: Raspberry Pi

change.what: Raspberry Pi goes on sale.

change.what: The first commercial chip-scale atomic clock goes on sale.

milestones.note: Precise timing for networks and substations without relying on satellites.

milestones.title: Neutral-atom quantum computers

research.what: Harvard, MIT and Paris researchers arrange atoms with optical tweezers.

change.what: A neutral-atom quantum computer becomes available on a public cloud.

milestones.note: A fast-moving alternative to superconducting qubits.

milestones.title: Wearable quantum brain scanner

research.what: University of Nottingham researchers use optically pumped magnetometers to measure brain activity.

change.what: The spin-out Cerca Magnetics commercialises the first OPM-MEG scanners.

milestones.note: UK quantum sensing reaching hospitals in about four years.

milestones.title: Quantum-secured metro network

research.what: Toshiba’s Cambridge Research Laboratory develops practical QKD systems.

change.what: BT and Toshiba launch a commercial trial of a quantum-secured network in London.

milestones.note: Real but specialised; post-quantum cryptography remains the main defence.

milestones.title: Two-factor authentication tokens

research.what: Security Dynamics is founded to build time-based authentication tokens.

change.what: SecurID tokens go on sale. Dates approximate.

milestones.note: The ancestor of every authenticator app.

milestones.title: CAPTCHA

research.what: Carnegie Mellon researchers invent tests that tell humans and computers apart.

change.what: reCAPTCHA launches; Google acquires it in 2009.

milestones.note: Now under pressure from AI that can solve them.

milestones.title: Trusted Platform Module

research.what: The Trusted Computing Platform Alliance forms to design hardware roots of trust.

change.what: TPM security chips ship in business PCs. Dates approximate.

milestones.note: Hardware trust anchors now required by Windows 11.

milestones.title: Differential privacy

research.what: Dwork and colleagues at Microsoft Research define differential privacy.

change.what: Differential privacy is deployed at scale in Apple’s iOS.

milestones.note: Lets data be shared for analysis without exposing individuals; relevant to smart meter data.

milestones.title: End-to-end encrypted messaging

research.what: Open Whisper Systems develops the Signal protocol.

change.what: WhatsApp turns on end-to-end encryption for over a billion users.

milestones.note: Security by default at global scale.

milestones.title: Hardware memory tagging

research.what: Arm announces its Memory Tagging Extension.

change.what: Memory tagging becomes available in consumer phones.

milestones.note: Hardware that blocks a whole class of memory-safety exploits.

milestones.title: Microwave radio relay

research.what: Bell Labs develops microwave relay links after wartime radar research.

change.what: Coast-to-coast microwave relay carries US telephone and television traffic.

milestones.note: Utilities later built their own microwave networks for control systems.

milestones.title: Text messaging (SMS)

research.what: Hillebrand and Ghillebaert propose short messages over GSM.

change.what: The first SMS is sent on Vodafone’s UK network.

milestones.note: Now used for outage alerts to customers.

adoption.what: Texting becomes mainstream in the UK.

milestones.title: Fibre to the home

research.what: BT Research at Martlesham develops passive optical networks.

change.what: Large-scale fibre-to-the-home services launch.

milestones.note: British research behind today’s full-fibre broadband.

milestones.title: Global satellite phones

research.what: Motorola announces the Iridium constellation.

change.what: Iridium satellite phone service begins.

milestones.note: Commercially troubled at first; now vital for remote and emergency work.

milestones.title: Software-defined networking

research.what: Stanford researchers publish OpenFlow.

change.what: Software-defined networks enter commercial and hyperscale use.

milestones.note: Networks became programmable, and so did their attack surface.

milestones.title: Li-Fi light communication

research.what: Professor Harald Haas at the University of Edinburgh demonstrates data over LED light.

change.what: The Edinburgh spin-out pureLiFi ships its first Li-Fi products.

milestones.note: A Scottish university invention.

milestones.title: Polyester fibre

research.what: Whinfield and Dickson at the Calico Printers’ Association, Manchester, invent polyester.

change.what: Commercial polyester fibre is produced in the US, then as Terylene in the UK.

milestones.note: A British invention now in most clothing.

milestones.title: Polycarbonate

research.what: Hermann Schnell at Bayer, and Daniel Fox at GE, independently make polycarbonate.

change.what: Commercial polycarbonate goes on sale.

milestones.note: Tough, clear plastic for meters, enclosures and safety equipment.

milestones.title: Superglue

research.what: Harry Coover at Eastman Kodak discovers cyanoacrylate, initially rejected as too sticky.

change.what: Eastman 910 goes on sale.

milestones.note: A failed experiment that found its product 16 years later.

milestones.title: OLED displays

research.what: Tang and VanSlyke at Kodak demonstrate efficient organic LEDs.

change.what: The first commercial OLED display ships in car audio.

milestones.note: Cambridge’s polymer LED work followed in 1989.

adoption.what: OLED screens become standard on flagship phones.

milestones.title: Gallium nitride power transistors

research.what: The first gallium nitride high-electron-mobility transistor is demonstrated.

change.what: Commercial GaN power transistors go on sale.

milestones.note: Smaller, more efficient chargers and power converters.

milestones.title: Aerogel insulation

research.what: Samuel Kistler makes the first aerogels.

change.what: Flexible aerogel insulation blankets reach the market. Dates approximate.

milestones.note: Seventy years waiting for affordable manufacturing.

milestones.title: Self-healing concrete

research.what: Henk Jonkers at Delft University uses bacteria that make limestone to seal cracks.

change.what: Commercial self-healing concrete products launch. Dates approximate.

milestones.note: Could extend the life of foundations and cable tunnels.

milestones.title: Commercial cargo to the space station

research.what: NASA’s Commercial Orbital Transportation Services programme funds private spacecraft.

change.what: SpaceX’s Dragon makes the first commercial cargo delivery to the ISS.

milestones.note: A government buying a service rather than owning the vehicle.

milestones.title: Commercial crew spaceflight

research.what: NASA begins its Commercial Crew Development programme.

change.what: Crew Dragon begins operational crew flights.

milestones.note: Ten years from contract to routine service.

milestones.title: Suborbital space tourism

research.what: SpaceShipOne wins the Ansari X Prize.

change.what: Virgin Galactic begins commercial suborbital flights.

milestones.note: Nearly twenty years: safety and certification set the pace.

milestones.title: Radar microsatellites

research.what: ICEYE spins out of Aalto University to build small radar satellites.

change.what: Commercial radar imagery from microsatellites goes on sale.

milestones.note: Day-and-night, all-weather monitoring of assets and flooding.

milestones.title: Methane-detecting satellites

research.what: GHGSat is founded to measure industrial emissions from orbit.

change.what: Its first satellite begins commercial methane monitoring.

milestones.note: Satellites now spot gas leaks from individual facilities.

milestones.title: Laser links between satellites

research.what: NASA’s lunar laser communication demonstration.

change.what: Laser inter-satellite links enter commercial broadband service. Dates approximate.

milestones.note: Faster links, and harder to intercept.

milestones.title: Underwater robots (ROVs)

research.what: The US Navy develops CURV remotely operated vehicles.

change.what: Commercial ROVs serve the offshore industry. Dates approximate.

milestones.note: Now used to lay and inspect subsea cables such as Eastern Green Link 1.

milestones.title: Robotic milking

research.what: Dutch publicly funded agricultural research develops automatic milking.

change.what: Lely sells the first commercial milking robot.

milestones.note: Farms automated before most factories outside cars.

milestones.title: Robotic lawn mowers

research.what: Husqvarna develops autonomous mowing.

change.what: The solar-powered Automower goes on sale.

milestones.note: Simple autonomy succeeds first.

milestones.title: Powered exoskeletons

research.what: Amit Goffer begins developing a walking exoskeleton.

change.what: ReWalk receives US approval for personal use.

milestones.note: Also being trialled to reduce strain for field engineers.

milestones.title: Sidewalk delivery robots

research.what: Starship Technologies is founded by Skype’s co-founders.

change.what: Commercial robot delivery begins in Milton Keynes.

milestones.note: A UK town became a testbed for everyday autonomy.

milestones.title: Streptomycin

research.what: Schatz and Waksman at Rutgers University discover streptomycin.

change.what: Streptomycin enters medical use against tuberculosis.

milestones.note: Nobel Prize 1952.

milestones.title: Medical ultrasound

research.what: Professor Ian Donald at the University of Glasgow begins ultrasound imaging in obstetrics.

change.what: The Diasonograph, the first commercial ultrasound scanner, is produced in Scotland.

milestones.note: A University of Glasgow invention now used in every hospital.

adoption.what: Ultrasound becomes routine in pregnancy care.

milestones.title: Contraceptive pill

research.what: Gregory Pincus begins hormonal contraception research.

change.what: The first oral contraceptive is approved.

milestones.note: Social change as much as medical.

milestones.title: Implantable pacemaker

research.what: Elmqvist and Senning implant the first pacemaker in Sweden.

change.what: Commercial implantable pacemakers go on sale.

milestones.note: Fast because the need was urgent and the device simple.

milestones.title: Beta blockers

research.what: James Black at ICI in Cheshire designs drugs to block adrenaline receptors.

change.what: Propranolol is launched.

milestones.note: A British discovery; Black shared the 1988 Nobel Prize.

milestones.title: Cochlear implant

research.what: Graeme Clark’s team at the University of Melbourne implants a multichannel device.

change.what: The multichannel cochlear implant is approved in the US.

milestones.note: University research created a global medical device company.

milestones.title: Cancer immunotherapy

research.what: James Allison’s team shows that blocking CTLA-4 unleashes immune attacks on tumours.

change.what: The first checkpoint inhibitor, ipilimumab, is approved.

milestones.note: Nobel Prize 2018.

adoption.what: Checkpoint inhibitors become a standard treatment for several cancers.

milestones.title: CAR-T cell therapy

research.what: Zelig Eshhar at the Weizmann Institute engineers chimeric antigen receptors.

change.what: The first CAR-T therapy is approved.

milestones.note: Living drugs took nearly 25 years.

milestones.title: Reversible pumped storage at scale

research.what: The North of Scotland Hydro-Electric Board develops a reversible pump-turbine scheme inside Ben Cruachan.

change.what: Cruachan, the world’s first large reversible pumped-storage station, opens.

milestones.note: Still one of GB’s largest stores of electricity.

milestones.title: Solar thermal power stations

research.what: Publicly funded US solar thermal research after the oil shocks.

change.what: The first commercial solar thermal power station enters service in California.

milestones.note: Overtaken by cheaper photovoltaics.

milestones.title: Wave power to the grid

research.what: Ocean Power Delivery, an Edinburgh company, develops the Pelamis wave energy converter.

change.what: Pelamis becomes the first offshore wave machine to supply a national grid.

milestones.note: A Scottish first; the company later failed, a reminder that physics is not the only hurdle.

milestones.title: Active network management

research.what: University of Strathclyde researchers develop automatic control of generation on constrained networks.

change.what: Orkney’s active network management scheme goes live via the Strathclyde spin-out Smarter Grid Solutions, connecting extra wind without new lines.

milestones.note: Saved an estimated £30m of reinforcement; all six GB distribution operators now use the approach.

milestones.title: Offshore wind HVDC connection

research.what: Developers design the first HVDC link for a far-offshore wind farm.

change.what: BorWin1 connects a North Sea wind farm to the German grid by HVDC.

milestones.note: The model for future deep-water wind connections.

milestones.title: Inkjet printer

research.what: Canon and HP independently develop thermal inkjet printing.

change.what: HP ThinkJet goes on sale.

milestones.note: Affordable printing for every desk.

milestones.title: Electronic paper displays

research.what: MIT Media Lab researchers develop electrophoretic electronic ink, spun out as E Ink.

change.what: The Amazon Kindle launches with an E Ink screen.

milestones.note: Ultra-low-power displays now used for shelf labels and signage.

milestones.title: Online retail

research.what: Jeff Bezos founds Cadabra, later Amazon.

change.what: Amazon.com begins selling books online.

milestones.note: Its spare computing capacity later became Amazon Web Services.

milestones.title: Online banking

research.what: Banks experiment with home banking over the Prestel videotex service.

change.what: Bank of Scotland launches HOBS, an early UK online banking service.

milestones.note: A Scottish first; now a major cyber target.

milestones.title: Body tracking without markers

research.what: Microsoft Research in Cambridge, UK, develops machine learning to track body pose from depth images.

change.what: Kinect launches for Xbox.

milestones.note: A UK research lab’s work in millions of homes within two years.

milestones.title: Autonomous AI diagnosis

research.what: University of Iowa research on automated diabetic eye disease detection.

change.what: IDx-DR becomes the first autonomous AI diagnostic system approved in the US.

milestones.note: Regulators had to decide how to approve a machine that diagnoses alone.

milestones.title: Scanning tunnelling microscope

research.what: Binnig and Rohrer at IBM Zurich use quantum tunnelling to image atoms.

change.what: Commercial scanning probe microscopes go on sale. Dates approximate.

milestones.note: Nobel Prize in Physics 1986; opened up nanotechnology.

milestones.title: Quantum cascade laser

research.what: Bell Labs demonstrates the quantum cascade laser.

change.what: Commercial quantum cascade lasers are sold for gas sensing.

milestones.note: Used to detect methane and other gases.

milestones.title: PGP email encryption

research.what: Phil Zimmermann releases Pretty Good Privacy.

change.what: PGP Inc. sells commercial encryption products.

milestones.note: Its author was investigated for exporting cryptography.

milestones.title: Onion routing (Tor)

research.what: The US Naval Research Laboratory develops onion routing.

change.what: The Tor anonymity network is released to the public.

milestones.note: Protects dissidents, and hides criminal infrastructure.

milestones.title: Fingerprint sensors on phones

research.what: Commercial research on silicon fingerprint sensors.

change.what: Fingerprint unlocking goes mainstream on smartphones.

milestones.note: Made biometrics an everyday security control.

milestones.title: Ethernet

research.what: Robert Metcalfe and colleagues invent Ethernet at Xerox PARC.

change.what: 3Com and others sell commercial Ethernet products.

milestones.note: Still the basis of most wired networks, including substations.

milestones.title: Data modems

research.what: Modems are developed for the US SAGE air defence network.

change.what: The Bell 103 modem goes on sale.

milestones.note: Remote telemetry for utilities grew from this.

milestones.title: Digital terrestrial television

research.what: European broadcasters and governments create the DVB standards.

change.what: The UK launches the world’s first digital terrestrial television service.

milestones.note: A UK world first that freed spectrum for mobile.

milestones.title: 3G mobile data

research.what: 3GPP finalises the first 3G standards.

change.what: The first commercial 3G network opens in Japan.

milestones.note: The start of the mobile internet.

milestones.title: Long-range low-power radio (LoRa)

research.what: French start-up Cycleo develops long-range spread-spectrum radio.

change.what: Semtech commercialises LoRa chips.

milestones.note: Used for low-cost sensors on networks.

milestones.title: Visible LEDs

research.what: Nick Holonyak at General Electric makes the first visible-light LED.

change.what: Commercial LED indicators and displays go on sale.

milestones.note: Half a century later, LEDs cut lighting energy use dramatically.

milestones.title: Electrochromic smart glass

research.what: Satyendra Deb demonstrates electrochromic films.

change.what: Commercial dimmable smart glass for buildings goes on sale. Dates approximate.

milestones.note: Cuts cooling energy in buildings.

milestones.title: Plant-based plastics

research.what: Cargill researches polylactic acid from corn.

change.what: NatureWorks opens commercial-scale PLA production.

milestones.note: Renewable feedstocks for plastics.

milestones.title: Satellite search and rescue

research.what: Canada, France, the US and the USSR agree to develop Cospas-Sarsat.

change.what: The satellite search and rescue system is declared operational.

milestones.note: Cold War rivals cooperating; tens of thousands of lives saved.

milestones.title: Autonomous mining trucks

research.what: Carnegie Mellon and Caterpillar research autonomous haulage.

change.what: Autonomous haulage trucks enter commercial mining operations.

milestones.note: Driverless heavy vehicles arrived in mines long before roads.

milestones.title: HPV vaccine

research.what: Ian Frazer and Jian Zhou at the University of Queensland make virus-like particles.

change.what: The first HPV vaccine is approved.

milestones.note: A vaccine that prevents cancer.

milestones.title: Targeted breast cancer antibody

research.what: Dennis Slamon at UCLA links HER2 to aggressive breast cancer.

change.what: Herceptin is approved.

milestones.note: Personalised medicine based on a tumour’s genetics.

milestones.title: Targeted leukaemia drug

research.what: Brian Druker at Oregon Health & Science University works with Ciba-Geigy on a kinase inhibitor.

change.what: Imatinib (Gleevec) is approved.

milestones.note: Turned a deadly leukaemia into a manageable condition.

milestones.title: Laser eye surgery

research.what: Researchers show excimer lasers can reshape the cornea.

change.what: LASIK is approved in the US.

milestones.note: Sixteen years through device approval.

milestones.title: Reinforcement-learning control room assistants

research.what: France’s RTE and INRIA launch the Learning to Run a Power Network challenges, where AI agents operate simulated grids; a 2023 track tests AI as an operator assistant.

change.what: AI assistants suggest congestion and switching actions to control engineers, with humans deciding. Estimated.

milestones.note: Research shows large cuts in redispatch; trust, explainability and safety cases are the gating factors.

milestones.title: Satellite AI vegetation management

research.what: AiDash develops AI that reads satellite imagery to predict tree growth near power lines.

change.what: Its vegetation management system is deployed by large utilities, including National Grid in the US.

milestones.note: Replaces some LiDAR and foot patrols with satellite monitoring.

milestones.title: Network-wide satellite AI tree management in GB

research.what: UK Power Networks’ Satelline pilot covers 400km of lines and about 3,500 spans with satellite imagery and AI.

change.what: Satellite and AI vegetation management used across whole GB distribution networks. Estimated.

milestones.note: The pilot found the approach highly accurate; a full business case is under way.

milestones.title: Vehicle-to-grid for households

research.what: Willett Kempton’s team at the University of Delaware proposes using parked electric cars to support the grid.

change.what: Octopus launches the UK’s first V2G tariff; a car, bidirectional charger and tariff bundle with BYD follows in 2025.

milestones.note: Twenty-seven years: it needed cars, chargers, standards and tariffs to line up.

milestones.title: AI home energy agents

research.what: Suppliers and start-ups apply AI agents to automate household heat pumps, batteries and EV charging.

change.what: Mainstream AI agents manage household energy automatically for price and grid signals. Estimated.

milestones.note: Raises consumer protection, cyber and data questions that Ofgem will need to address.

milestones.title: Machine learning battery lifetime prediction

research.what: Stanford, MIT and Toyota Research Institute show machine learning can predict battery life from the first few cycles.

change.what: Commercial battery analytics platforms use machine learning to forecast degradation. Dates approximate.

milestones.note: Cuts months of testing from battery development and helps storage owners plan.

milestones.title: AI-discovered electrolyser catalysts

research.what: The Open Catalyst Project releases large datasets and models to search for catalysts for green hydrogen.

change.what: An electrolyser using an AI-discovered catalyst reaches the market. Estimated.

milestones.note: Catalysts are a major cost in green hydrogen.

milestones.title: AI management system standard

research.what: ISO and IEC set up a joint committee on artificial intelligence standards.

change.what: ISO/IEC 42001, the first certifiable AI management system standard, is published.

milestones.note: Gives organisations, including energy companies, an auditable framework for AI governance.

milestones.title: Assured AI in operational energy decisions

research.what: Regulators and system operators begin defining assurance for AI used in operations.

change.what: AI systems approved through sector assurance to act in live energy operations with human oversight. Estimated.

research.what: UK SMR competition and Rolls-Royce SMR design work begin.

research.what: Research shows coordinated wake steering of turbines raises wind farm output.

change.what: AI-coordinated wind farm control is standard on new offshore wind farms. Estimated.

milestones.note: Software-only gains from existing hardware.
